candidates.classification: source-level apparent conflict with governing movement rule in strategic encounter escape calculation; supported choice change and runtime behavior unverified
candidates.rule: Root AGENTS.md Combat legibility requires combat performance to use total incapacitation rather than fatigue directly, and states that neither fatigue nor total incapacitation adds a movement-speed penalty before incapacitation; physical mass and limb effects remain separate. Applying this rule to the strategic encounter escape-speed estimate is an explicit review interpretation: the estimate is not a tactical movement simulation, but controls a combat encounter response.
candidates.detail: The current encounter path computes the maximum living party fatigue percentage from calories used and injury-adjusted endurance, then core sustainable_speed_m_per_minute directly scales the party speed by 10,000 minus 50 basis points per fatigue percent. Independently, party_encumbrance_remaining_basis_points multiplies carrying capacity by 0.5 for Staggered and 0 for Incapacitated, although Staggered is a total incapacitation greater than 0.5 but less than 1.0. The calculated speed is stored and used for run availability and run rejection; it is an abstract strategic escape calculation, not a measured tactical movement speed. The route and narrative paths both reach the speed builder, and the random encounter commit recalculates it after movement. No product code or user action was run.
candidates.source_derived_example: For a single ready traveler on a road with an assumed 90 kg total body-plus-inventory burden, 450 kg leg-derived capacity and 8,000 remaining burden basis points, the integer formula yields 66 m/min at 0% fatigue and 61 m/min at 15% fatigue. With healthy chest-adjusted endurance 2 and 300 calories used, the same source gives fatigue ratio 0.15; fatigue_incapacitation is zero below 0.5, and with other impairment zero the strategic status is Ready. Holding physical inputs and zero fatigue fixed but assuming status Staggered, the capacity becomes 225 kg, remaining burden becomes 6,000 basis points and the formula yields 49 m/min. These are exact source-formula counterexamples under stated inputs, not a claim that a particular generated journey, threat, roll, client or player reaches them. In particular no supported road-and-enemy speed threshold crossing has been established.
candidates.safeguards: The calculation includes actual body and inventory mass, injury-adjusted leg strength, party logistics and terrain, which may be legitimate physical effects and must not be discarded. Full incapacitation remains a distinct gate, and the web template displays a speed-comparison reason when running is unavailable. Separate condition and wheel projections, actual threat/terrain distributions and all encounter entry points have not been exhaustively traced; this does not assert hidden factors or a runtime incident.
candidates.connected_scope: CharacterStats fatigue and strategic incapacitation owners, ready/staggered/incapacitated projection, real physical burden and limb capacity, core strategic encounter speed and run eligibility, random travel and authored narrative materialization, route terrain, native encounter storage, UI and any tactical movement consumers. Scope the movement rule to the abstract strategic estimate explicitly before implementing.
candidates.proposed_repair: After complete policy and caller discovery, remove the direct fatigue and pre-incapacitation status multipliers from encounter speed if the governing movement rule covers this escape estimate, while preserving intentional physical-mass, limb, terrain, party and incapacitation behavior. Do not introduce a second fatigue pool or a compatibility path.
candidates.later_acceptance: After product validation is authorized, verify two otherwise identical non-incapacitated states do not acquire a different encounter speed solely from fatigue or total incapacitation; verify physical mass and limb effects, full-incapacitation behavior, intended encounter options, strategic/tactical boundary and player-facing explanation remain correct.
